newsitem.title: JAPAN: Key points of Japan Big Bang insurance proposals.
newsitem.headline: Key points of Japan Big Bang insurance proposals.

text.p: Following are the main points of a final report released on Friday by Japan's Insurance Council, an advisory panel to the Finance Minister, proposing deregulation of Japan's insurance markets.
The proposals were made to help Japan set a schedule for implementing its "Big Bang" financial market reforms.
The report from the panel will be adopted as is by the ministry, Finance Ministry officials said.

*Insurance companies should be allowed, via subsidiaries, to enter into other financial businesses, and other financial institutions should be allowed to enter the insurance business via subsidiaries by the end of 2001.
*Insurance companies should be allowed to enter the banking, trust banking and securities businesses earlier than 2001.
*Securities firms' entry into the insurance business should be allowed earlier than 2001, and the purchase of failed insurance firms by banks and trust banks should also be allowed earlier than 2001.
*Holding companies for financial services should be introduced after steps are taken to ensure protection of policyholders and to ensure the financial health of insurance companies.
*Insurance companies owned by policyholders should not be allowed to set up holding companies. Only insurance firms owned by shareholders should be allowed to do so.
*Banks should be allowed to sell long-term fire and life insurance policies from 2001. Both of these are required when taking out a mortgage.
*Beginning in July 1998, non-life insurers should no longer be obliged to follow tariffs set by an industry body for voluntary auto, fire and casualty insurance.
*Mark-to-market accounting methods should be implemented as soon as possible in appraising insurance firms' trading accounts.
